A3.reason: One reader <-> one bank cannot be expressed for an INTERLEAVED ROW_MAJOR source, for any bank count. An interleaved page lives in bank `page_id % num_banks`; tilize's work unit is a tile-row = TILE_H CONSECUTIVE source sticks = TILE_H consecutive page ids, whose residues mod any num_banks > 1 are distinct. So every reader that produces even one tile touches min(TILE_H, num_banks) banks, and no work assignment fixes that without abandoning the tile. The ~92%-of-peak recipe in Saturating_DRAM_bandwidth.md needs a bank's worth of data RESIDENT per core — that is lever C15 (prefer sharded), already applied in Refinements 1-2. The Phase-0 predicted 35% was ALSO refuted on the target itself: the 288 GB/s datasheet peak is unreachable here. A pure DRAM->DRAM copy of the same tensors (examples/dram_saturation, no compute kernel at all) measures 87,710 ns @64 cores on [1,1,2048,2048] bf16, 12,078 ns on [1,1,32,16384], 174,772 ns on [1,1,8192,1024] — i.e. ~192 GB/s, and tilize now runs at or below those numbers.

B8.reason: [write-side twin knob: write_trid — arms test_bench_lever_write_trid_off / test_bench_lever_both_trid_off] Trid double-issue is BUILT on both halves (reader and writer): block i's transfers are issued before block i-1's barrier, so a request is always in flight across the block boundary. Measured NULL on every regime that can show it (<=1.5%, both signs, inside the +-3% band), including the B0 smallest-regime check on [1,1,32,64]. The cause is measured, not argued: (a) and (c) already run at or below a pure DRAM->DRAM copy of the same tensor, so extra in-flight requests cannot buy bandwidth the DRAM interface will not deliver, and (b) has one block per core so there is no next block to double-issue against. Both levers are correct (bit-exact under --dev) and regression-free, so they are KEPT rather than reverted. NOTE for anyone re-enabling this family: a trid left on the WRITE command buffer halts BRISC in firmware after kernel_main returns (brisck.cc:91 ASSERT(ncrisc_noc_packet_tags_cleared)); it presents as a whole-grid hang at waypoint NKFW, not as a CB deadlock. Reset the trid to 0 before exit.

C16.reason: Depth-2 CBs are kept because the public API mandates use_double_buffer=True as the default and the L1 cost is bounded by the CB budget — but they buy nothing measurable, and Refinement 3 established WHY, refuting Phase 0's explanation. Phase 0 said 'the op is DRAM-bound so the reader cannot run ahead'; the real reason was that the grid-filling square landed ONE block per core, leaving the second CB slot with nothing to hold. Refinement 3's pipeline knob gives that shape 4 blocks per core and won 1.077x — and C16 is STILL flat at 4 blocks/core (86,457 depth-2 vs 86,579 depth-1). F24.reason: bfp8_pack_precise ships at its CHEAP setting (False = the fast, truncating block-float packer) and the expensive arm was measured for the first time this phase. Both directions are inside the noise band on this op: fast 65,253 / precise 64,981 ns on the grid-filling square (-0.4%) and fast 2,930 / precise 3,008 ns on the smallest regime (+2.7%, the B0 per-core-overhead check). That is the DM bound talking - tilize is 88-95% data movement, so an extra pack pass hides in the DRAM shadow and the knob cannot pay either way. The decision is therefore made on ACCURACY, and the fast packer already clears the gate from both inputs: measured PCC 0.99997 (bf16 -> bf8b) and 1.00000 (fp32 -> bf8b) against the pad oracle, vs a 0.99 threshold - so there is no margin to buy. Note this refutes the skill's own anchor for tilize (`~1.4x slower at identical cores`): that ratio is a pack-bound measurement, and this op is not.

F25.reason: fp32_dest_acc_en (+ UnpackToDestFp32 on the input CB) is enabled ONLY when the datums really are 32-bit on both sides (fp32 -> fp32), which is exactly F25's rule. It is what makes that transition bit-exact rather than tf32-truncated; every other dtype pair leaves DEST cheap. | Refinement 4 adds a SECOND, non-negotiable arm: a 1-byte datum (uint8). The tilize LLK's 8-bit path (ckernel_defs.h IS_8BIT_FORMAT) is only validated with DEST accumulation on, and with a 16-bit DEST the packed tile comes out ALL ZEROS (measured: probes/probe_021.py, 8159/8192 elements wrong). So on that dtype fp32 DEST is a CORRECTNESS requirement, not a precision preference, and it has no keepable off arm - it is pinned structurally instead by test_uint8_requires_fp32_dest. The gate is on the DTYPE, not on element_size(): bfloat8_b also reports 1 byte per element and must NOT take the 8-bit path.

notes.L4_split_reader: Design lamp L4 (master.md example T2 `split_reader`, ~1.7x) becomes APPLICABLE for the first time with Refinement 1: on a sharded-OUTPUT plan the writer issues no NoC work at all, so BRISC is free to take half the reader's DRAM reads on the interleaved->shard crossover. Not built here (Refinement 1 is placement only); it is Refinement 3's business. It has no Part-2 catalog ID, hence this note rather than a levers row.
notes.phase1_stale_closure_reread: The 10 'possibly unlocked' staleness signals are the topology block moving from interleaved-only to interleaved + three sharded plan paths. Re-read at Refinement 1 and all still hold: A1 (row_wise) is INAPPLICABLE on the sharded path (cores come from shard order, split_work_to_cores is not called); A4 (cliff cores) — derive_shard_blocking makes WT_CHUNK divide shard_wt exactly and uneven shards fall back to the accessor path; B11 — a shard row is shard_w*elem with shard_w % 32 == 0, still a 32 B multiple; B12 — destination tile regions are disjoint, so even the cross-core gather reads no byte twice; C16 — an aliased CB has no depth and the zero-copy path is compute-bound (ablation: 4901 -> 862 with compute stubbed), so there is still nothing to overlap; C17 — RM-in / TILE-out still cannot alias (the two aliased CBs sit on different tensors); D20/F23/F26/F27 are untouched by placement.
notes.R2_xfer_gate: Refinement 2 added the `xfer_gate` knob (LEVERS, default 1) with both arms in _bench_tilize.py (test_bench_lever_xfer_gate, test_bench_lever_xfer_gate_narrow_destination). It decides whether aliasing the DESTINATION shard is worth the read transfer the shard's width pins: 1.66x / 3.21x in favour of the grid split below the 256 B knee, no effect above it (dram->HEIGHT x8, 512 B reads: 7,983 vs 8,058 ns). It never gates a SOURCE-local plan — the writer always moves whole TILE pages, measured 0.94x (2 cores) to 3.85x (8 cores). Mechanism-wise this is B5 (transaction size) crossed with A2 (core placement); it has no catalog ID of its own.
notes.R2_reshard_retarget: Re-target for the reshard rows: with the destination local there is NO write traffic, so the ceiling is the SOURCE shard's L1 egress (2 cores x 256 KB in 256 B transfers ~= 14 GB/s/core), not the DRAM floor. Ablation on [1,1,1024,256] WIDTHx2->HEIGHTx8: full 18,487 -> no_compute 17,615 (-4.7%) -> sync_only 745 ns, i.e. DM-bound (95%). Remaining headroom is the source-side fan-in, which the CALLER picks (shard spec), plus L4 split_reader — now MORE applicable than at Refinement 1, since on a destination-local gather BRISC does no NoC work at all.
notes.phase2_stale_closure_reread: The 10 staleness signals at Refinement 2 are the topology block gaining three plan paths (padded-into-local-shard, the paged cross-spec gather, and that gather on the full grid). Re-read, and all still hold: A1 (row_wise) — still not called on a shard-pinned plan, and the GATED gather does call split_work_to_cores again but over the same round-robin DRAM/L1 page map where it measured as noise; A4 (no cliff width) — derive_shard_blocking still divides the shard width exactly, and Refinement 2's uneven grids split ROWS, not W, so the short last shard is a cliff in H that the per-shard block count absorbs (no second kernel width); B11 (32 B transactions) — now stronger, since every page slice of the gather is a 32 B multiple by construction and the one geometry that would break it is refused (test_unaddressable_shard_row_is_refused); B12 (no mcast/semaphores) — still zero, now asserted per-descriptor in test_reshard_placement_and_source_page_geometry; C16 (double_buffer) and D20 (regime_select) — unchanged on the interleaved rows they were measured on, though both now have a new consumer (the gather streams through the input CB and forces R_PAD), so they are the two rows most worth re-measuring in a perf phase; C17 / F23 / F26 / F27 — the format, precision-knob and arithmetic facts they rest on did not move.
notes.phase3_pipeline_lever: NEW non-catalog lever `pipeline` (PIPELINE_BLOCKS_PER_CORE / MIN_PIPELINE_READ_BYTES): the block derivation now targets several blocks per core instead of stopping at the grid-fill floor, capped so a read transfer never drops below the B5 floor. Both constants are SWEPT, not chosen: blocks/core 1/2/4/8/16 -> 94,398 / 85,846 / 85,122 / 88,444 / 87,298 ns on [1,1,2048,2048] bf16 (4 wins, and fp32 agrees within 0.25%); MIN_PIPELINE_READ_BYTES 128/256/512/1024 -> 15,076 / 14,092 / 13,964 / 13,150 ns on [1,1,32,16384] bf16 (monotonic, so the cap correctly refuses to split that shape finer). Whole-refinement A/B (n=7 medians): [1,1,2048,2048] bf16 92,608 -> 86,235 (-6.9%), fp32 195,738 -> 181,230 (-7.4%). Both arms in _bench_tilize.py (`pipeline`, plus `pre_r3` = every Refinement-3 lever off at once).
notes.phase3_ceiling_retarget: The DRAM-floor target the queue quoted (288 GB/s -> 58.3 us on [1,1,2048,2048]) is a datasheet number this box cannot reach for an interleaved DRAM->DRAM stream. Measured practical ceiling with examples/dram_saturation (pure copy, NO compute kernel): 87,710 ns @64c / 86,943 @32c on 2048x2048 bf16 (191-193 GB/s), 12,078 @64c / 11,550 @32c on 32x16384, 174,772 @64c on 8192x1024. tilize now measures 86,235 / 13,606 / 171,695 ns — i.e. 1.01x, 0.89x and 1.02x of a pure copy of the same bytes. Use these, not 288 GB/s, as the target.
notes.phase3_split_dm_ablation: New ABLATE keys dm_read / dm_write attribute the wall to each NoC half. bf16: (a) full 86,594 | no_reads 59,482 | no_writes 43,930; (b) 12,721 | 9,364 | 8,155; (c) 169,518 | 122,680 | 93,055. The WRITE half is the larger one everywhere, which is why B8's writer twin was built rather than shipping a reader-only lever.
notes.phase4_stale_closure_reread: Refinement 4 moves the topology in three ways (a new element WIDTH family down to 1 byte, rank 0, and the writer's optional OUTPUT-format pad stamp in a new shared header), so all 13 negative closures were re-read before their topology stamps were refreshed. All still hold, and one needed real re-checking rather than a glance: B11 (alignment) is the only row a NARROWER element could break, because the aligned read chunk is WT_CHUNK*32*elem - at 1 byte/elem the smallest possible chunk is one tile column = 32 B, exactly the DRAM alignment, so it still cannot go under. test_b11_every_transaction_is_dram_aligned is now parametrized over all three widths (1/2/4 B) to keep that pinned. The rest are untouched by an element width: A1/B10 are placement and VC, A3's page->bank residue argument is dtype-free, A4's exact-divisor W split is unchanged, B12 (nothing is read twice) and C17 (RM-in/TILE-out cannot alias) are properties of the permutation itself, C16/D20 were measured on the interleaved path this phase did not touch, F23 (no caller-supplied precision knob) still holds - tilize still exposes no ComputeKernelConfig - and F26/F27 (lossless unpack, math fidelity) are untouched: uint8 gets fp32 DEST but still Fp32Mode::Fast, and the op still does no arithmetic.
notes.R4_out_fill: Refinement 4 added the `out_fill` knob (LEVERS, default 1) with both arms in _bench_tilize.py (test_bench_lever_out_fill). It is a CORRECTNESS mechanism, not a perf lever - it is what makes a padded WIDENING cast exact, so its off arm has no correct output on the cells it governs - but it is benched because it is the most expensive thing this refinement adds. Worst-case geometry ([1,1,1024,2048] -> [1,1,2048,2048] bf16 -> fp32, half the output tiles are WHOLE pad tiles): 386,033 ns with the stamp vs 187,130 without, i.e. 2.06x. The stamp is 2 M fp32 rv32 volatile L1 word stores at ~10 cycles each; two things were measured on it. (1) Filling the LARGEST contiguous runs the tiled face geometry allows (face-first instead of row-first) is FLAT - the cost is the store COUNT, not loop overhead. (2) Skipping the reader's now-redundant input-format fill on this path (identical fill region, and the writer's word is the exact one) is worth 28.6%: 540,314 -> 386,033 ns. Remaining idea, NOT built: stamp one tile then replicate it with local L1->L1 noc_async_write, which would trade ~1024 stores per whole-pad tile for one 4 KB NoC transfer. It needs a scratch buffer and puts the writer's NoC on a path that currently has none, and the cells that reach the stamp at all are narrow (a bf16 -> fp32 pad whose fill is not bf16-representable - 10.2 yes, 0.0 / 3.5 / -18.0 / -32.5 all exact and therefore stamp-free).
notes.R4_gate_is_the_lever: The `out_fill` gate (needs_output_format_fill: quantize the fill through the input format, then through the output format, and compare against quantizing straight to the output format) is what keeps the 2.06x off every other cell. It is pinned by test_out_fill_gate_fires_only_when_the_round_trip_loses_the_fill over 9 dtype/fill combinations, plus test_out_fill_is_off_on_the_unpadded_hot_path, so the unpadded and same-format paths stay byte-identical to Refinement 3's kernels.
notes.R5_tile_geometry: Refinement 5. TINY TILES needed no kernel change (every byte quantity already derived from tile_h) beyond one host gap: ttnn.allocate_tensor_on_device's shape/dtype/layout overload has no tile= parameter, so the output tensor silently carried a 32x32 tile; the TensorSpec overload fixes it. Measured on a_square bf16: tile_h 32/16/8/1 = 86,359 / 89,594 / 95,941 / 249,925 ns. The cost is inherent to the requested geometry (a 1x32 tile packs 32x as many tiles for the same bytes), and tile_h=32 is unchanged, so no supported shape regressed. On the d_smallest overhead regime a tiny tile is FASTER (tile_h=8: 1,815 vs 2,896 ns) because the finer tile-row grid spreads 8 blocks over more cores. RETILE is DM-shaped but L1-STORE-bound, like Refinement 4's pad stamp: the reader stages whole source tile pages (a face row is 16 elements = 32 B at bf16, 16 B at uint8, below the 32 B / 64 B DRAM read alignment on WH / BH, so face rows are NOT addressable in DRAM) and then moves each face row with rv32 word copies. Measured [1,1,1024,1024] bf16: 32->8 99,252 ns, 1->32 124,631 ns, 32->16 101,475 ns (~42 GB/s vs ~190 GB/s for the row-major path). NOT built, recorded for the perf tournament: a retile is a pure FACE permutation, so it could bypass the row-major round trip entirely and copy contiguous face-row RUNS page-to-page (min(in_tile_h, tile_h)*16 elements per run, e.g. 512 B for 32->16 instead of 32 copies of 32 B), with compute reduced to a pass-through. That is a scheme change (the input CB would hold tiled data, not sticks), not a knob.
notes.phase5_stale_closure_reread: verify_levers --phase 5 flags 14 negative closures as possibly-unlocked because the topology block gained the tile-height axis and the two R_RETILE plan paths. Every one was re-read against the new paths and still holds: A1 (row_wise) / A4 (no cliff-core width) / B11 (32 B-multiple transfers) / B12 (no operand read by two cores) — the tile height only scales the tile-row count and the page size, and a retile's transfers are whole tile PAGES, which are page-aligned and read by exactly one core. A3 (one reader ↔ one bank) is still structurally impossible and for the SAME reason on the retile path: an interleaved page lives in bank page_id % num_banks and a block spans consecutive pages. B8 (trid double-issue) and B10 (per-reader VC) stay as measured — the retile wall is the local rv32 face permutation, not the NoC (staging is one whole-page read per source tile), so a NoC-issue lever has nothing to shorten there. C16 (depth-2 CBs) unchanged: the retile stage is depth-1 reader-private scratch and the streaming CBs keep their depth. C17 (input and output can never alias) needed the closest look, because a retile is the FIRST case where both tensors are TILE layout: it still holds, since the op allocates a distinct output tensor and the retile reader has already staged and permuted the source bytes before the packer writes. D20 (compile-time regime selector) now selects among THREE regimes rather than two, which strengthens rather than changes it. F23/F24/F26/F27 are precision rows and tile geometry does not touch them (F24's own arm was re-measured at Refinement 4 and bfloat8_b x tile_height=16 is now an EXCLUSION, so the block-float surface got smaller, not larger).
